web_evidence.title: The Fifth Witness Excerpt
web_evidence.note: The author's authorized, sustained excerpt from Chapters One and Two has Mickey Haller narrating his actions, perceptions, history, and client relationship as I/my.

web_evidence.title: The Fifth Witness Reading Guide
web_evidence.note: The official guide says its questions cover the entire book and reproduces first-person statements attributed to Mickey from the case, his family relationships, and the ending.

web_evidence.title: Book review: The Fifth Witness by Michael Connelly
web_evidence.note: A contemporaneous review explicitly identifies the Mickey Haller novels, including this reviewed volume, as first-person narratives and contrasts them with the third-person Bosch series.

search_log: Searched “Michael Connelly The Fifth Witness excerpt first chapter” and opened the authorized excerpt on the author's website.

Searched the author's site for The Fifth Witness excerpt, reading guide, audiobook material, and Q&A; the audiobook page identified only the performer, while the excerpt and reading guide supplied usable prose evidence.
Searched “The Fifth Witness first person narrator” and “The Fifth Witness point of view Mickey Haller”; opened the explicit Petrona review and checked weaker review results.

Searched the Los Angeles Times, Publishers Weekly, and Kirkus for narration descriptions; available results mainly summarized the plot or called Haller the narrative focus without explicitly establishing grammatical person.

Searched for alternating narration, epistolary form, diaries, frames, and multiple narrators; found no credible indication that The Fifth Witness departs from Mickey Haller's first-person base narration.
person_note: The Goodreads evidence repeatedly exposes Mickey Haller as the participating I-narrator in actions, perceptions, legal strategy, and personal history. The authorized opening independently sustains the same voice, while the official whole-book reading guide samples Mickey's first-person statements through later events and the ending; an explicit contemporaneous review confirms the Haller narration is first person. Generic you passages are advice rather than second-person storytelling, and third-person references merely describe other characters within Mickey's narration. No evidence of sustained sections in another person was found.
